title: Dedicated capacity incident: isolation controls, reservation sizing, and burst-policy action plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2026-03-10 we experienced a ~45-minute capacity degradation across 3 Dedicated clusters in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 that increased latency and caused transient request failures for some reserved customers. Root causes identified: (1) noisy-neighbor processes consuming disproportionate GPU memory and KV cache slots, (2) several customer reservations were under-sized relative to observed peak steady-state working set (reservation mis-sizing), and (3) our burst admission policy allowed short-lived high-concurrency bursts that exhausted GPU slots and admission tokens before autoscaling could react.

Impact: ~12% of reserved requests experienced >=2x latency increase, 3 customers reported degraded SLAs (two on Dedicated Bronze, one on Dedicated Gold). Unit cost spiked during the event due to emergency burst capacity.

Detection & timeline: Alerts fired 2026-03-10 02:17 UTC (queue depth +10% over SLO), mitigations kicked at 02:25 UTC (soft-throttles), partial rollback of burst admission at 02:34 UTC, full stabilization at 03:02 UTC after targeted isolation of noisy jobs and temporary reservation ramp-ups.

Technical root causes:
- Noisy neighbor: one multi-tenant job on cluster A created long-lived KV cache growth, occupying ~42% of available KV slots, causing frequent cache evictions and OOM errors on colocated tasks. Our scheduler did not detect cache imbalance as a resource pressure signal.
- Reservation mis-sizing: reservation sizing tool relied on 7-day P95 token rates; several reservations had been created with optimistic working sets ~30% below real peak due to recent model rollout changes.
- Burst policy tuning: current burst admission uses a simple token bucket per-cluster with no adaptive backoff for consecutive bursts; we observed cascading short bursts from several customers that depleted admission tokens faster than autoscaler ramp-up (autoscaler cooldown = 120s).

Action items (concrete, owners, acceptance criteria):
1) Implement noisy-neighbor detection metric and automated soft-isolation (eviction/backpressure) for KV-cache-heavy sessions. Owner: Diego Morales. Estimate: 3 points. Due: 2026-03-28. Acceptance: alerts trigger when a session holds >30% KV slots and automated soft-isolation reduces cluster-wide cache eviction rate by >=60% in canary. Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1423.
2) Reservation sizing re-run and new policy: build a reservation re-sizing job that recomputes recommended reservation sizes based on 14-day window + model-change multiplier. Owner: Lin Chen. Estimate: 3 points. Due: 2026-03-25. Acceptance: <10% of reservations flagged as underprovisioned when compared to new policy in two sample clusters. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CAP/Reservation+Sizing+Design.
3) Adaptive burst gate: modify burst admission to include adaptive backoff and per-customer burst debt accounting to prevent repeated short bursts from overwhelming clusters. Owner: Marcus Rivera. Estimate: 5 points. Due: 2026-04-01. Acceptance: in load test, adaptive gate yields no more than 10% extra admission variance vs baseline and prevents admission exhaustion in simulated 50% concurrent short-burst workload.
4) Capacity playbook updates & runbook automation: update on-call runbooks to include noisy-neighbor isolation steps, temporary reservation bump commands, and a quick checklist for burst rollback. Owner: SRE (Elena Ortiz). Estimate: 2 points. Due: 2026-03-18. Acceptance: runbook reviewed by SRE + Eng and validated in tabletop drill. Runbook doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CAP/Dedicated+Capacity+Playbook.
5) Telemetry improvements: add KV-cache occupancy, per-session GPU mem pressure, and burst-token usage metrics to the dedicated-capacity dashboard; create pre-SLO alerts at 70% thresholds. Owner: Observability (Ravi Shah). Estimate: 2 points. Due: 2026-03-22. Acceptance: dashboards populated and alert firing simulated in staging. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abc123/dedicated-capacity-incident.
6) Customer communication & SLA review: PM to draft customer notices for affected orgs and update expectation pages for Dedicated bursts. Owner: PM (Nora Feldman). Due: 2026-03-16. Acceptance: notices sent and support summaries posted to internal portal.

Trade-offs considered: immediate hard isolation risks evicting healthy jobs; chosen path uses soft-isolation/backpressure to reduce blast radius. Rapidly tightening burst gate reduces short-term latency variance but may penalize legitimate short-burst workloads; plan includes a canary rollout with per-customer whitelisting.

Longer-term recommendations: explore MIG-like instance partitioning for stronger tenant isolation and quota boundaries, and incorporate model-version-aware reservation forecasts during scheduled rollouts.

Links & artifacts: Postmortem doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CAP/ENG-4932+Postmortem; Incident dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abc123/dedicated-capacity-incident; Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1423; internal notes: gs://redwood-inc/incidents/2026-03-10-dedicated-capacity/
updates: 2026-03-11 — Initial triage completed. Root cause hypotheses drafted (noisy neighbor + reservation sizing). Notified PM and SRE. (Aisha)
2026-03-12 — Reproduced KV-cache growth pattern in staging using synthetic workload. Confirmed that soft-isolation can reduce eviction rate. (Diego)

2026-03-13 — Design review with Observability and SRE: agreed on new metrics and thresholds. PR #1423 created for runtime soft-isolation prototype. (Design feedback: add per-customer annotation for visibility)
2026-03-14 — Decision: pursue soft-isolation + reservation re-sizing + adaptive burst gate in parallel. Prioritized telemetry and runbook updates first. (PM sign-off: Nora Feldman)
acceptance_criteria: Noisy-neighbor automations run in staging and reduce cluster-level cache eviction by >=60%
Reservation re-sizing flags underprovisioned reservations for manual review with <10% false positive rate in sample clusters
Adaptive burst gate prevents admission exhaustion in synthetic burst storms while preserving >=90% of normal admission rates for non-abusive customers
Runbook updated and validated by SRE in tabletop exercise
